title: Finite quotient realization preserves the actual smooth-exchange mate
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, and the integral adic datum d of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. For a chosen cartesian square h : Y to X, e : Y to T, f : X to S, g : T to S and any n >= 0, let M be any object of the derived category of modules over the actual nth quotient coefficient sheaf on T. The arrow sbcFiniteExchangeApp of [lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange] at M is isomorphic, in the arrow category over the quotient-coefficient derived category on X, to pbcDerivedFunctionRealization_X applied to the fixed-scalar pro-etale derivedBaseChangeMap for the flipped square at the inverse realization of M. The realization is the canonical function-coefficient realization of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], and the fixed-scalar operations are those of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. No smoothness, noetherianity, boundedness, completeness or etale-origin assumption is imposed.

proof.text: The locally bijective constant-scalar presentation supplies the exact equivalence pbcFunctionRealization at every corner. The characterization of pbcLevelConstantComparison on constant sections identifies its scalar unit with pbcFunctionScalars. The adjunct of completedFiniteCoefficientMap is the constant direct-image map conjugated by these level comparisons. Thus direct image followed by restriction of the scalar action evaluates on exactly the same object and has exactly the fixed scalar action. Identity on sections yields the normalized direct-image comparison, as in the existing finite coefficient realization/direct-image theorem. The coefficient-ring presentation is transported by the canonical finiteRingComparison.

proof.text: Conjugate these right-adjoint comparisons across the exact realization equivalences, using the normalized tensor adjunctions, to obtain the left-adjoint comparisons and their unit and counit equations. Direct-image composition is given by restriction along the canonical fiber-product pasting arrow. Both composites of sectionwise comparisons therefore agree. Uniqueness of adjoints identifies the corresponding pullback compositors. Derive the exact equivalences and the pullbacks termwise; equivalences preserve K-injective resolutions, so the right-derived direct-image comparisons are isomorphisms. The normalized K-flat characterization of the ringed pullback compositor and the fixed-scalar derived comparators identify the two derived squares.

proof.text: Expand both exchange maps as unit followed by the pullback square followed by the counit. Substitute the three normalized comparison equations from step 2. Functoriality and naturality identify the composites. The source and target comparison isomorphisms give an isomorphism of arrows. The counit of the realization equivalence at M changes the chosen fixed-scalar representative to the inverse of pbcDerivedFunctionRealization at M. No geometric, boundedness or etale-origin assumptions are used, and the constant-section identities also apply to the zero ring and empty schemes.

lean.statement:
theorem sbcFiniteExchange_encoding
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    {X S T Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S} {g : T ⟶ S} {h : Y ⟶ X} {e : Y ⟶ T}
    (sq : ChosenCartesianSquare h e f g) (n : ℕ)
    (M : DerivedCategory
      (pbcModules T ((pbcAdicRings T (pbcIntegralDatum l E)).obj (op n)))) :
    Nonempty (Arrow.mk (sbcFiniteExchangeApp l E sq n M) ≅
      Arrow.mk ((pbcDerivedFunctionRealization X (pbcIntegralDatum l E) n).map
        ((ProEtale.derivedBaseChangeMap
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ProEtale.PbcQuotient (pbcIntegralDatum l E) n))
          sq.toCommSq.flip).app
            ((pbcDerivedFunctionRealization T (pbcIntegralDatum l E) n).asEquivalence.inverse.obj
              M))))
